*Auto-generated daily digest from the [AI/CyberSec Hub](/ai-sec-hub/). Summaries are AI-assisted; always check the linked sources.*

Today's stories center on AI-accelerated offense: Swiss authorities confirmed agentic attacks hit critical infrastructure, and broader threat roundups show extension and server hijacking trends. Defensive themes include keeping security metrics operational and funding AI data-risk tooling.

## Swiss Authorities Confirm AI-Assisted Intrusions
Swiss cyber authorities report that AI-agent-driven intrusions succeeded in four of five confirmed attacks, including against critical infrastructure operators. Agentic attacks are now a real-world threat that defenders need to plan for.

Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/switzerland-confirms-ai-assisted.html)

## ThreatsDay: Exposed NGINX, Rogue Extensions, AI Server Hijacking
This weekly roundup covers roughly 10 million exposed NGINX services, over 250 malicious browser extensions, and hijacking of AI servers. It also notes extensions that behave differently depending on how they are installed.

Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/threatsday-250-rogue-extensions-10m.html)

## Keeping Your Security Picture Current Against AI-Speed Attackers
The piece argues that many security metrics exist for presentation rather than action. It recommends current, operational measures that reflect real environment conditions as attackers move faster with AI.

Source: [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/11/how-to-keep-your-security-picture.html)

## Matters.AI Raises Record Pre-Series A in India
The Indian startup raised what is described as the country's largest cybersecurity pre-Series A round. Its platform merges four legacy tools and uses context-aware AI to track sensitive data and auto-remediate threats.

Source: [Dark Reading](https://www.darkreading.com/cyber-risk/matters-india-cybersecurity-pre-series-ai-data-risks)

## Schneier: Outages Have Economic Causes
Schneier argues that a cluster of major outages across tech, aviation, banking, and government systems stems from economic underinvestment in infrastructure. Resilience, in his view, is a funding and incentive problem as much as a technical one.

Source: [Schneier on Security](https://www.schneier.com/blog/archives/2026/11/recent-outages-have-economic-causes.html)

## Takeaways
- Agentic attacks have moved from theory to confirmed incidents; plan detection and response accordingly.
- Audit browser extensions and exposed services such as NGINX and AI servers, which are active attack surfaces.
- Favor operational, current security metrics over presentation-oriented ones.
